# Commentary on Manifesto of the Communist Party (CM)

Generated from `commentary/` and `renderings/`. Each tradition writes in its own files; see docs/commentary-guide.md.

## CM I.23.2 · "Idiocy of rural life" is a mistranslation of Idiotismus

**General (no particular tradition)** · Translation note · status: proposed · `general:idiotismus-is-isolation`

The German Idiotismus does not mean idiocy (Idiotie). Hal Draper argued that it carries the sense of the Greek
idiotes, a private person cut off from public life, and translated the phrase as "the privatized isolation of
rural life". The 1888 English, which Engels approved, has "idiocy", and that rendering is the source of the
common claim that Marx despised peasants.

Sources:
- Hal Draper, The Adventures of the Communist Manifesto (1994; Haymarket 2020), note to paragraph 28
- Hal Draper, Karl Marx's Theory of Revolution, vol. 2 (1978), pp. 344ff.

See also: CM I.23.3

## CM II.66.1-II.79.1 · In 1872 Marx and Engels said the end of Section II was dated, and drew a lesson about the state from the Paris Commune

**General (no particular tradition)** · Later theory (revises) · status: proposed · `general:authors-revise-the-ten-measures`

In their 1872 preface the authors say they lay no special stress on the revolutionary measures at the end of
Section II (CM P1872.2.3) and that the passage would be worded very differently by then (CM P1872.2.4). The reasons they give
are the growth of large-scale industry and the experience of 1848 and the Paris Commune (CM P1872.2.5). They add
that the Commune proved that the working class cannot simply lay hold of the ready-made state machinery and use
it for its own purposes (CM P1872.2.6). Every tradition reads that sentence against CM II.66.1, and reads it
differently; those readings belong in each tradition's own commentary, answering this entry.

By: CM P1872.2.3; CM P1872.2.4; CM P1872.2.5; CM P1872.2.6

Sources:
- Marx and Engels, Preface to the German edition of 1872 (MEW 18, pp. 95-96)
- Marx, The Civil War in France (1871), section III

See also: CM P1888.10.5
